sentences.text: ?Court No. - 85
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 12968 of 2022

Applicant :- Suresh Kumar Gaud @ Manju
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjay Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ranjeet Asthana
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Sanjay Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ranjeet Asthana, learned counsel for the first informant, Sri O.P. Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 0175 of 2022, under Sections 376, 504, 506, 323 IPC and Section 66-E of I.T. Amendment Act, 2008, Police Station Cantt., District Prayagraj.

4. As per prosecution case, the first informant/victim had family relations with the accused; it is alleged in the FIR that her husband fell sick and during that period, the applicant frequently used to visit her and he, in October 2021 committed rape on her and took some objectionable photos;
thereafter on the basis of this photographs, he started blackmailing her and several times committed rape on her; on 03.07.2022, he again attempted rape and when the first informant-the victim protested, he extended threats to her husband's and kid's life; it is alleged in the FIR that the accused, his brothers and his wife are now pressurizing her to settle the matter between themselves.

5. It is contended on behalf of the applicant that he is absolutely innocent; the real fact is that the applicant's wife lodged a complaint against the husband of the informant; it is mentioned in the Suresh Kumar Gaud @ Manju vs State Of U.P. on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7618851/
1 complaint that they had family relations since last 12 years and have been partner in some business transactions also

entities.text: Suresh Kumar Gaud @ Manju vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ; out of some dispute the first informant threatened them to entangle in a false case; it is further contended that even if the allegations as contained in the FIR are looked into, it becomes quite clear that relations between the two have been consensual in nature and now the FIR has been lodged for certain ulterior motives.

6. The application for anticipatory bail is opposed by the other side on the premises that the first informant/victim in her statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has corroborated the FIR version.
It is conceded that there is unexplained long delay in lodging the FIR.
No medical examination has been conducted.

7. In case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by the Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In the instant case, I considered submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case.
In my view, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.

entities.text: Suresh Kumar Gaud @ Manju vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.
11. It is made clear that observations made herein shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion at any stage of the case based on material before him.
